meanings: I Ching; Book of Changes (abbr. for 易經|易经[Yi4 jing1])

example.hanzi: 写汉字不容易。
example.pinyin: Xiě Hànzì bù róngyì.
example.english: Writing Chinese characters is not easy.
example.fact: Standard Chinese uses thousands of characters, and even educated native speakers typically recognize only a few thousand of them in daily use.

etymologyHint: The first rays 十 of the sun 日

components.note: 日 (sun) — represents the sun.
十 depicts the first rays of sunlight appearing low on the horizon — together with 日 (sun) giving 早 its meaning 'early, morning.'

example.hanzi: 很多老人早上去公园锻炼。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō lǎorén zǎoshang qù gōngyuán duànliàn.
example.english: Many elderly people go to the park to exercise in the morning.
example.fact: In China, many older adults have a daily habit of doing group exercise, such as tai chi, in public parks early in the morning.

etymologyHint: A rice cooker on heat 日, building up steam 丷 and letting it off

components.note: Originally pictured a container for steaming food: 日 at the bottom represents the heat or cooking vessel, and 丷 at the top shows the steam rising and escaping — giving 曾 its meaning 'once, already.'

example.hanzi: 孔子曾经是老师。
example.pinyin: Kǒngzǐ céngjīng shì lǎoshī.
example.english: Confucius was once a teacher.
example.fact: Confucius was a real teacher and philosopher in ancient China whose ideas have influenced Chinese culture for more than two thousand years.

etymologyHint: The waste 余 produced by a city 阝

components.note: 阝 (a mound/settlement) — represents a city or town.
余 (surplus, remainder) — the leftover waste a city produces, which must be cleared away, giving 除 its meaning 'to remove, eliminate.'

example.hanzi: 除了中国,亚洲还有很多国家。
example.pinyin: Chúle Zhōngguó, Yàzhōu hái yǒu hěn duō guójiā.
example.english: Besides China, Asia has many other countries.
example.fact: Asia is the world's largest continent by both area and population, made up of dozens of countries.

etymologyHint: Simplified form of 農, tilling the field 田 with a hoe 辰

components.note: 农 is the simplified form of 農, which depicted using a hoe 辰 to till a field 田 — an image of farming that gave rise to the meaning 'agriculture.'

example.hanzi: 以前,很多中国人是农民。
example.pinyin: Yǐqián, hěn duō Zhōngguó rén shì nóngmín.
example.english: In the past, many Chinese people were farmers.
example.fact: For most of Chinese history, the majority of the population worked as farmers in rural areas.

etymologyHint: To go searching with a spear 戈 in hand 扌

components.note: 扌 (hand) — represents an action performed by hand.
戈 (a spear/dagger-axe) — an old image of searching or probing with a weapon in hand, giving 找 its meaning 'to search, to look for.'

example.hanzi: 很多人去美国找金子。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō rén qù Měiguó zhǎo jīnzi.
example.english: Many people went to America to look for gold.
example.fact: In the 1800s, large numbers of people moved to America during gold rushes, hoping to find gold and get rich.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — 装 relates to clothes, dress, and attire
壮 (zhuàng) gives the sound — 装 is pronounced zhuāng, a close match

example.hanzi: 京剧演员的服装很漂亮。
example.pinyin: Jīngjù yǎnyuán de fúzhuāng hěn piàoliang.
example.english: Peking opera performers' costumes are very beautiful.
example.fact: Peking opera is a traditional Chinese art form famous for its colorful costumes, painted faces, and stylized singing.

meanings: "house on a cliff" radical in Chinese characters (Kangxi radical 53), occurring in 店, 序, 底 etc
etymologyHint: A lean-to 厂, suggesting a building

components.note: 广 depicts a lean-to shelter built against a wall or cliff, open on one side — the image behind its meaning 'wide, spacious' and its use as the 'building' radical.

example.hanzi: 天安门广场很大。
example.pinyin: Tiān'ānmén Guǎngchǎng hěn dà.
example.english: Tiananmen Square is very big.
example.fact: Tiananmen Square in Beijing is one of the largest public squares in the world.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 显 relates to something bright and clearly visible in the light
业 (yè) gives a loose sound connection to 显's reading xiǎn

example.hanzi: 显微镜可以显示很小的东西。
example.pinyin: Xiǎnwēijìng kěyǐ xiǎnshì hěn xiǎo de dōngxi.
example.english: Microscopes can show extremely small things.
example.fact: Microscopes allow scientists to see tiny things, such as cells and bacteria, that are far too small for the human eye to see alone.

meanings: bar (loanword) (serving drinks, or providing Internet access etc)
abbr. for 貼吧|贴吧[tie1 ba1]

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 吧 is a spoken particle, tied to speech and the mouth
巴 (bā) gives the sound — 吧 is pronounced ba, a related (unstressed) form of the same sound

example.hanzi: 我们走吧。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zǒu ba.
example.english: Let's go.
example.fact: 吧 is a sentence-final particle that softens a suggestion or command in Mandarin, roughly like 'let's' or 'shall we' in English; it has no independent meaning outside this grammatical role.

meanings: prefix used before monosyllabic names, kinship terms etc to indicate familiarity
(bound form) Afghanistan (abbr. for 阿富汗[A1 fu4 han4])
(bound form) Albania (abbr. for 阿爾巴尼亞|阿尔巴尼亚[A1 er3 ba1 ni2 ya4])
(bound form) Algeria (abbr. for 阿爾及利亞|阿尔及利亚[A1 er3 ji2 li4 ya4])
(bound form) Argentina (abbr. for 阿根廷[A1 gen1 ting2])

components.note: 阝 (a mound/place) — reflects 阿's original meaning related to a hill or slope
可 (kě) gives a sound close to 阿's reading ā

example.hanzi: 他叫阿明。
example.pinyin: Tā jiào Ā Míng.
example.english: His name is A-Ming.
example.fact: 阿 is a friendly prefix Chinese speakers add before a name or family title, such as 阿姨 ('auntie'), to sound warm and familiar.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 李 is the plum tree, a type of fruit tree
子 (zǐ) gives a sound close to 李's reading lǐ

example.hanzi: 李是中国很常见的姓。
example.pinyin: Lǐ shì Zhōngguó hěn chángjiàn de xìng.
example.english: Li is a very common surname in China.
example.fact: Li (李) is consistently one of the most common family names in China, shared by tens of millions of people.

meanings: stand the bole of a tree
to mark with a symbol, label, lettering etc

components.note: 木 (wood/tree) — 标 originally referred to the tip of a tree, later coming to mean 'mark, sign'
票 (piào) gives a sound close to 标's reading biāo

example.hanzi: 中国的目标是探索太空。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó de mùbiāo shì tànsuǒ tàikōng.
example.english: China's goal is to explore space.
example.fact: China has its own national space program, which has sent astronauts into orbit and spacecraft to the Moon.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 谈 relates to talking, conversation
炎 (yán) gives a sound close to 谈's reading tán

example.hanzi: 《论语》是孔子和学生的谈话记录。
example.pinyin: 《Lúnyǔ》 shì Kǒngzǐ hé xuéshēng de tánhuà jìlù.
example.english: The Analects is a record of conversations between Confucius and his students.
example.fact: The Analects, one of the most famous books in Chinese history, is a collection of conversations between Confucius and his students.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 吃 relates to eating, done with the mouth
乞 (qǐ) gives a sound close to 吃's reading chī

example.hanzi: 中国人喜欢吃米饭。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó rén xǐhuan chī mǐfàn.
example.english: Chinese people like to eat rice.
example.fact: Rice is a staple food for more than half of the world's population, and it has been grown in China for thousands of years.

etymologyHint: Simplified form of 圖; a map of a district's 啚 borders 囗

components.note: 图 is the simplified form of 圖, which pictured a district's borders 啚 enclosed within a boundary 囗 — an old image of a map, giving 图 its meaning 'picture, chart, map.'

example.hanzi: 长城在中国地图上很长。
example.pinyin: Chángchéng zài Zhōngguó dìtú shàng hěn cháng.
example.english: The Great Wall looks very long on the map of China.
example.fact: The Great Wall of China is one of the longest structures ever built, stretching for thousands of kilometers across northern China.

meanings: variant of 念[nian4], to read aloud
etymologyHint: To keep the present 今 in mind 心

components.note: 今 (now, the present) — represents what is currently on one's mind.
心 (heart/mind) — keeping the present moment in mind gave 念 its meaning 'to think of, to read aloud, to study.'

example.hanzi: 中秋节,人们会想念家人。
example.pinyin: Zhōngqiūjié, rénmen huì xiǎngniàn jiārén.
example.english: At the Mid-Autumn Festival, people miss their families.
example.fact: The Mid-Autumn Festival is a major Chinese holiday associated with family reunion, so it's a time when people who are apart often think fondly of their families.

example.hanzi: 六在中国是吉利的数字。
example.pinyin: Liù zài Zhōngguó shì jílì de shùzì.
example.english: Six is a lucky number in China.
example.fact: In Chinese culture, the number six is considered lucky because it sounds like words related to smoothness and good fortune.

etymologyHint: To pull back a bow's 弓 drawstring 丨

components.note: 弓 (bow) — the weapon being drawn.
丨 depicts the taut drawstring being pulled back — giving 引 its meaning 'to pull, draw out, attract.'

example.hanzi: 长城每年吸引很多游客。
example.pinyin: Chángchéng měi nián xīyǐn hěn duō yóukè.
example.english: The Great Wall attracts many tourists every year.
example.fact: The Great Wall is one of the most visited historical sites in the world, drawing millions of tourists every year.

components.note: 厤 (relating to the sequence of time) — 历 relates to history and the calendar
力 (lì) gives the sound — 历 is pronounced lì, an exact match

example.hanzi: 中国的历史很长。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó de lìshǐ hěn cháng.
example.english: China's history is very long.
example.fact: China has one of the longest continuous civilizations in the world, with written records going back thousands of years.

etymologyHint: A deer's head 自 adorned with antlers 丷

components.note: 自 here depicts a head (the character also independently means 'nose, self').
丷 depicts hair atop the head — 首 originally pictured a head with hair, giving its meaning 'head, chief, first.'

example.hanzi: 东京是日本的首都。
example.pinyin: Dōngjīng shì Rìběn de shǒudū.
example.english: Tokyo is the capital of Japan.
example.fact: Tokyo is the capital of Japan and one of the most populous cities in the world.

components.note: 矢 (arrow) — 医 originally related to treating arrow wounds, the root of its meaning 'to cure, doctor'
匸 gives a loose sound connection to 医's reading yī

example.hanzi: 中医有很长的历史。
example.pinyin: Zhōngyī yǒu hěn cháng de lìshǐ.
example.english: Traditional Chinese medicine has a very long history.
example.fact: Traditional Chinese medicine, including practices like herbal remedies and acupuncture, has been practiced in China for thousands of years.

meanings: classifier for games: match, set, round etc
etymologyHint: A place where measures 尺 are discussed 口

components.note: 尺 (a ruler/measure) — represents rules or measures being set.
口 (mouth) — measures being discussed aloud in one place gave 局 its meaning 'bureau, office, situation.'

example.hanzi: 世界上很多国家都有邮局。
example.pinyin: Shìjiè shàng hěn duō guójiā dōu yǒu yóujú.
example.english: Many countries around the world have post offices.
example.fact: Post offices exist in almost every country and have long been the traditional way to send letters and packages.

etymologyHint: A dog 犬 rushing out of a cave 穴

components.note: 穴 (a cave/hole) — the den the dog bursts from.
犬 (dog) — a dog suddenly darting out of its den gave 突 its meaning 'sudden, abrupt.'

example.hanzi: 地震常常突然发生。
example.pinyin: Dìzhèn chángcháng tūrán fāshēng.
example.english: Earthquakes often happen suddenly.
example.fact: Earthquakes are notoriously hard to predict, so they always strike suddenly, without warning.

meanings: for a particular person, occasion, purpose

example.hanzi: 华佗是古代有名的医学专家。
example.pinyin: Huàtuó shì gǔdài yǒumíng de yīxué zhuānjiā.
example.english: Hua Tuo was a famous medical expert in ancient times.
example.fact: Hua Tuo was a real physician in ancient China, remembered as one of the earliest surgeons in Chinese medical history.

components.note: 贝 (shell/money) — 费 relates to spending money, fees, and expenses
弗 (fú) gives a loose sound connection to 费's reading fèi

example.hanzi: 在中国,义务教育是免费的。
example.pinyin: Zài Zhōngguó, yìwù jiàoyù shì miǎnfèi de.
example.english: In China, compulsory education is free.
example.fact: China provides nine years of free, compulsory education for all children, covering primary and junior middle school.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 号 relates to calling or crying out aloud, as well as a spoken or marked sign
丂 gives a loose sound connection to 号's reading hào

example.hanzi: 十月一号是中国的国庆节。
example.pinyin: Shí yuè yī hào shì Zhōngguó de Guóqìngjié.
example.english: October 1st is China's National Day.
example.fact: China's National Day, celebrated on October 1st, marks the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949.

meanings: (when used before a noun of location) furthest or extreme
to be within the limits of

example.hanzi: 我们要尽量节约用水。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yào jǐnliàng jiéyuē yòng shuǐ.
example.english: We should save water as much as possible.
example.fact: Fresh water is a limited resource — only a small fraction of all the water on Earth is fresh, and much of that is frozen in glaciers and ice caps.

example.hanzi: 这是我的杯子,那是另一个。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de bēizi, nà shì lìng yí gè.
example.english: This is my cup, that is another one.
example.fact: 另 is used before a noun or measure word to mean 'another, a different one' — as in 另一个 (lìng yí gè), 'another one.'

etymologyHint: Border 冂 around land 土 with a well 口

components.note: 冂 depicts a boundary or border enclosing an area.
土 (earth/land) — the land enclosed within the border.
口 here depicts a well within that land — together giving 周 its early meaning of a bounded territory, and later 'circumference, week, the Zhou dynasty.'

example.hanzi: 周朝是中国历史上很长的朝代。
example.pinyin: Zhōu Cháo shì Zhōngguó lìshǐ shàng hěn cháng de cháodài.
example.english: The Zhou dynasty was a very long dynasty in Chinese history.
example.fact: The Zhou dynasty is traditionally considered the longest-lasting dynasty in Chinese history, spanning many centuries.

components.note: 车 (cart/vehicle) — 较 originally related to comparing the crossbars of chariots
交 (jiāo) gives a sound close to 较's reading jiào

example.hanzi: 长江比较长。
example.pinyin: Chángjiāng bǐjiào cháng.
example.english: The Yangtze River is relatively long.
example.fact: The Yangtze River is the longest river in Asia and one of the longest rivers in the world.

meanings: (bound form) to pour into; to flow into; to inject
(bound form) to focus (one's spirit, gaze etc) on a single point; to concentrate

components.note: 氵 (water) — 注 relates to pouring or directing, like water poured into something
主 (zhǔ) gives a sound close to 注's reading zhù

example.hanzi: 司马光小时候很注意学习。
example.pinyin: Sīmǎ Guāng xiǎo shíhou hěn zhùyì xuéxí.
example.english: As a child, Sima Guang paid great attention to his studies.
example.fact: Sima Guang was a real historical scholar and statesman in ancient China, famous for compiling one of the greatest works of Chinese history.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 语 relates to language, words, and speech
吾 (wú) gives a loose sound connection to 语's reading yǔ

example.hanzi: 很多人说汉语。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō rén shuō Hànyǔ.
example.english: Many people speak Chinese.
example.fact: Mandarin Chinese has more native speakers than any other language in the world.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 仅 relates to a person or amount limited to just this much, giving its meaning 'only, merely'

example.hanzi: 熊猫仅生活在中国。
example.pinyin: Xióngmāo jǐn shēnghuó zài Zhōngguó.
example.english: Pandas live only in China.
example.fact: Wild giant pandas are found only in China, mainly in a few mountain ranges in the country's southwest.

components.note: 耂 (a variant of 老, 'old') — 考 relates to careful examination and testing
丂 gives a loose sound connection to 考's reading kǎo

example.hanzi: 古代中国人考试来当官。
example.pinyin: Gǔdài Zhōngguó rén kǎoshì lái dāngguān.
example.english: In ancient China, people took exams to become government officials.
example.fact: For over a thousand years, ancient China selected its government officials through a nationwide exam system called the imperial examinations.

components.note: 艹 (grass/plant) — 落 relates to leaves or plants falling
洛 (luò) gives the sound — 落 is also pronounced luò, an exact match

example.hanzi: 秋天,叶子会落下来。
example.pinyin: Qiūtiān, yèzi huì luò xiàlai.
example.english: In autumn, leaves fall.
example.fact: Many trees drop their leaves in autumn as days grow shorter and colder, a process called deciduous leaf fall.

meanings: short name for Qinghai 青海[Qing1 hai3]

example.hanzi: 青藏高原非常高。
example.pinyin: Qīng-Zàng Gāoyuán fēicháng gāo.
example.english: The Qinghai-Tibet Plateau is extremely high.
example.fact: The Qinghai-Tibet Plateau is one of the highest and largest plateaus on Earth, which is why it's nicknamed 'the roof of the world.'

etymologyHint: To walk 迶 to the city 阝; to follow a path

components.note: 阝 (a mound/city) — represents a place being traveled to.
迶 depicts walking or moving along a path — following someone to the city gave 随 its meaning 'to follow, along with.'

example.hanzi: 船员跟随郑和去了很多地方。
example.pinyin: Chuányuán gēnsuí Zhènghé qùle hěn duō dìfang.
example.english: The sailors followed Zheng He to many places.
example.fact: Zheng He was a real Ming dynasty admiral who led large fleets on long sea voyages, reaching as far as Africa.

components.note: 辶 (to walk/move) — 选 relates to the process of selecting, as if moving through options
先 (xiān) gives a sound close to 选's reading xuǎn

example.hanzi: 奥运会的主办城市是选出来的。
example.pinyin: Àoyùnhuì de zhǔbàn chéngshì shì xuǎn chūlái de.
example.english: The host city of the Olympics is chosen through a vote.
example.fact: The host city for the Olympic Games is chosen by International Olympic Committee members through a voting process.

components.note: 刂 (a knife, related to 刀) — cutting and arranging pieces in order ties to 列's meaning 'row, line, to arrange'

example.hanzi: 中国的高铁列车很快。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó de gāotiě lièchē hěn kuài.
example.english: China's high-speed trains are very fast.
example.fact: China has built the largest high-speed rail network in the world, with trains that can travel very fast between major cities.

etymologyHint: To stop someone 止 with an arrow 弋

components.note: 弋 (a dagger-axe/weapon) — represents military force.
止 (foot/to stop) — stopping an enemy by force of arms gave 武 its meaning 'military, martial.'

example.hanzi: 少林寺的和尚会武术。
example.pinyin: Shàolínsì de héshang huì wǔshù.
example.english: The monks of Shaolin Temple know martial arts.
example.fact: Shaolin Temple in China is world-famous as a birthplace of Chinese martial arts, especially Shaolin kung fu.

meanings: used in 女紅|女红[nu : 3 gong1]

components.note: 纟 (silk/thread) — 红 originally described a color of dyed silk, hence 'red'
工 (gōng) gives a loose sound connection to 红's reading hóng

example.hanzi: 在中国文化里,红色代表好运。
example.pinyin: Zài Zhōngguó wénhuà lǐ, hóngsè dàibiǎo hǎoyùn.
example.english: In Chinese culture, red represents good luck.
example.fact: Red is considered a lucky color in Chinese culture and is used often during festivals, weddings, and the Lunar New Year.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 响 relates to sound, something that can be heard
向 (xiàng) gives a loose sound connection to 响's reading xiǎng

example.hanzi: 过年,庙里的钟声很响。
example.pinyin: Guònián, miào lǐ de zhōngshēng hěn xiǎng.
example.english: At New Year, the temple bell rings loudly.
example.fact: Many Chinese Buddhist temples ring a large bell at midnight on New Year's Eve, a tradition believed to drive away bad luck for the coming year.

example.hanzi: 熊猫虽然是黑白的,但是很可爱。
example.pinyin: Xióngmāo suīrán shì hēibái de, dànshì hěn kě'ài.
example.english: Although pandas are black and white, they are very cute.
example.fact: Giant pandas are known worldwide for their distinctive black-and-white fur, a color pattern that is unique to them among bears.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 推 relates to pushing something with the hand
隹 (zhuī) gives a loose sound connection to 推's reading tuī

example.hanzi: 你推东西,东西才会动。
example.pinyin: Nǐ tuī dōngxi, dōngxi cái huì dòng.
example.english: Only when you push something does it move.
example.fact: This reflects a basic law of physics described by Isaac Newton: a still object needs a push or pull, a force, to start moving.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 势 relates to power, force, and influence
执 (zhí) gives a loose sound connection to 势's reading shì

example.hanzi: 打太极拳的姿势很重要。
example.pinyin: Dǎ tàijíquán de zīshì hěn zhòngyào.
example.english: Posture is very important when practicing tai chi.
example.fact: Tai chi is a traditional Chinese practice that combines slow, controlled movements with careful posture, and it's still widely practiced for health today.

components.note: 彡 (shān) is the historical phonetic component of 参; sound change over time has left little resemblance to the modern reading cān

example.hanzi: 很多国家参加奥运会。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō guójiā cānjiā Àoyùnhuì.
example.english: Many countries participate in the Olympics.
example.fact: The modern Olympic Games bring together athletes from nearly every country in the world to compete every four years.

example.hanzi: 希腊是奥运会的发源地。
example.pinyin: Xīlà shì Àoyùnhuì de fāyuándì.
example.english: Greece is the birthplace of the Olympics.
example.fact: The Olympic Games began in ancient Greece, and the modern Olympics still honor that origin with traditions like the torch relay.

etymologyHint: Words passing through ten 十 mouths 口

components.note: 十 (ten) — suggests something repeated many times.
口 (mouth) — a story passed down through ten generations of mouths gave 古 its meaning 'old, ancient.'

example.hanzi: 兵马俑是很古老的文物。
example.pinyin: Bīngmǎyǒng shì hěn gǔlǎo de wénwù.
example.english: The Terracotta Warriors are very ancient artifacts.
example.fact: The Terracotta Army, discovered by farmers digging a well, consists of thousands of life-sized clay soldiers buried over two thousand years ago to guard an emperor's tomb.

meanings: abbr. for 眾議院|众议院[Zhong4 yi4 yuan4], House of Representatives
etymologyHint: Three people 人 representing a crowd

components.note: 人 (person), tripled — three people together depict a crowd, giving 众 its meaning 'many, multitude.'

example.hanzi: 春节联欢晚会有很多观众。
example.pinyin: Chūnjié Liánhuān Wǎnhuì yǒu hěn duō guānzhòng.
example.english: The Spring Festival Gala has a huge audience.
example.fact: China's annual Spring Festival Gala, broadcast on Lunar New Year's Eve, is watched by an enormous audience, making it one of the most-watched television broadcasts in the world.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 构 relates to building structures, originally from wooden framing
勾 (gōu) gives a sound close to 构's reading gòu

example.hanzi: 中国古代建筑的结构很特别。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó gǔdài jiànzhù de jiégòu hěn tèbié.

example.fact: Traditional Chinese wooden buildings often used an interlocking bracket structure that could hold together without any nails.

components.note: 户 (door) — 房 relates to a room or house, a space behind a door

example.pinyin: Běijīng de hútòng yǒu hěn duō lǎo fángzi.

example.fact: Hutongs are narrow traditional alleyways in Beijing lined with old courtyard houses, some dating back hundreds of years.

etymologyHint: A cow 牛 splitting 丷 wood in half

components.note: 牛 (ox/cow) — cattle were used to help split or divide things such as firewood.
丷 depicts two small pieces splitting apart — giving 半 its meaning 'half.'

example.hanzi: 地球有两半,北半球和南半球。
example.pinyin: Dìqiú yǒu liǎng bàn, běi bànqiú hé nán bànqiú.
example.english: The Earth has two halves: the Northern Hemisphere and the Southern Hemisphere.
example.fact: The Earth is divided into two halves called hemispheres — the Northern Hemisphere and the Southern Hemisphere.

meanings: see 節骨眼|节骨眼[jie1 gu5 yan3]
etymologyHint: Simplified form of 節; sections of bamboo ⺮

components.note: 节 is the simplified form of 節, which depicted the segmented sections of a bamboo stalk ⺮ — giving 节 its meaning 'joint, section, festival.'

example.hanzi: 春节是中国最重要的节日。
example.pinyin: Chūnjié shì Zhōngguó zuì zhòngyào de jiérì.
example.english: Spring Festival is China's most important festival.
example.fact: Spring Festival, also called Chinese New Year, is the most important traditional holiday in China, marked by family reunions and fireworks.

etymologyHint: A lump of clay on a potter's wheel

components.note: 土 depicts a mound of earth resting on the ground — a simple picture of soil, giving 土 its meaning 'earth, soil, land.'

example.hanzi: 黄土高原的土是黄色的。
example.pinyin: Huángtǔ Gāoyuán de tǔ shì huángsè de.
example.english: The soil of the Loess Plateau is yellow.
example.fact: The Loess Plateau in northern China is covered in yellow soil, which gives the nearby Yellow River its distinctive color and name.

meanings: to throw (sth in a specific direction: ball, javelin, grenade etc)

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 投 relates to throwing something with the hand
殳 (shū) gives a loose sound connection to 投's reading tóu

example.hanzi: 端午节,人们把粽子投进江里。
example.pinyin: Duānwǔjié, rénmen bǎ zòngzi tóu jìn jiāng lǐ.
example.english: At the Dragon Boat Festival, people throw rice dumplings into the river.
example.fact: The Dragon Boat Festival is linked to the legend of the poet Qu Yuan, and throwing rice dumplings into the river is said to commemorate him.

etymologyHint: The sweet 甘 fruit of a certain tree 木

components.note: 甘 (sweet) — describes the fruit's taste.
木 (tree) — the sweet fruit of an unspecified tree gave 某 its meaning 'a certain, some.'

example.hanzi: 他住在某个城市。
example.pinyin: Tā zhù zài mǒu ge chéngshì.
example.english: He lives in a certain city.
example.fact: 某 is used before a noun to mean 'a certain, some particular' one, when the speaker doesn't specify exactly which one — similar to saying 'a certain city' in English.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 案 originally referred to a wooden table or desk
安 (ān) gives a sound close to 案's reading àn, differing only in tone

example.hanzi: 包公很会破案。
example.pinyin: Bāo Gōng hěn huì pò àn.
example.english: Bao Gong was very good at solving cases.
example.fact: Bao Gong (Bao Zheng) was a real Song dynasty official famous for his fairness, and he later became a legendary figure in Chinese folklore as a brilliant detective.

meanings: short name for Heilongjiang 黑龍江|黑龙江[Hei1 long2 jiang1]
etymologyHint: A man's face blacked by soot from a fire 灬

components.note: 黑 pictures a face or window blackened by soot rising from a fire 灬 below — giving 黑 its meaning 'black, dark.'

example.hanzi: 黑洞里没有光。
example.pinyin: Hēidòng lǐ méiyǒu guāng.
example.english: There is no light inside a black hole.
example.fact: A black hole's gravity is so strong that not even light can escape from it, which is why it appears completely black.

meanings: abbr. for Uyghur 維吾爾|维吾尔[Wei2 wu2 er3]

components.note: 纟 (thread/silk) — 维 relates to a connecting thread or fiber, extended to mean 'to maintain, to link'
隹 (zhuī) gives a loose sound connection to 维's reading wéi

example.hanzi: 水果里有很多维生素。
example.pinyin: Shuǐguǒ lǐ yǒu hěn duō wéishēngsù.
example.english: Fruits contain many vitamins.
example.fact: Vitamins are nutrients the human body needs in small amounts to stay healthy, and fruits are one of the best natural sources of them.

components.note: 革 depicts an animal hide being stretched out and worked — the picture behind its meaning 'hide, leather, to reform.'

example.hanzi: 改革开放以后,中国发展很快。
example.pinyin: Gǎigé kāifàng yǐhòu, Zhōngguó fāzhǎn hěn kuài.
example.english: After Reform and Opening-up, China developed quickly.
example.fact: China's Reform and Opening-up policy, started in the late 1970s, transformed the country's economy and led to rapid growth.

example.hanzi: 中国有五年计划。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó yǒu wǔ nián jìhuà.
example.english: China has Five-Year Plans.
example.fact: China organizes its economic and social goals into Five-Year Plans, a practice that has continued for decades.

meanings: (bound form) to be a match for; to rival

components.note: 攵 (to strike) — 敌 relates to conflict and opposition, as with an enemy

example.pinyin: Sūnzǐ shuō, yào liǎojiě zìjǐ de dírén.
example.english: Sunzi said that you must understand your enemy.
example.fact: Sunzi's Art of War is an ancient Chinese military text, written over two thousand years ago, that is still studied today for its strategic wisdom.

meanings: (literary) to send; to transmit; to convey

components.note: 攵 (an action/to strike) — ties to 致's sense of bringing about or causing an effect

example.hanzi: 全球变暖会导致海平面上升。
example.pinyin: Quánqiú biànnuǎn huì dǎozhì hǎipíngmiàn shàngshēng.
example.english: Global warming leads to rising sea levels.
example.fact: As global temperatures rise, melting ice and expanding warm water are causing sea levels to rise around the world.

meanings: Chen (c. 1045 – 479 BC), a Zhou dynasty state
etymologyHint: To place 阝 facing east 东

components.note: 阝 (a mound/place) — represents a location or settlement.

example.hanzi: 在台湾,陈是很常见的姓。
example.pinyin: Zài Táiwān, Chén shì hěn chángjiàn de xìng.
example.english: In Taiwan, Chen is a very common surname.
example.fact: Chen (陈) is one of the most common surnames in southern China and Taiwan.

etymologyHint: To walk 彳 as required by law 聿

components.note: 彳 (to walk/step) — represents movement or conduct.
聿 (an old form related to a writing brush) — conduct guided by written rules gave 律 its meaning 'law, regulation.'

example.pinyin: Měi ge guójiā dōu yǒu zìjǐ de fǎlǜ.
example.english: Every country has its own laws.
example.fact: Legal codes have existed in China for thousands of years; the Tang dynasty's legal code was one of the most influential in East Asian history.

etymologyHint: The leg 口 above the foot

components.note: 足 depicts a leg (the upper shape) above a foot — a simple picture of the human leg and foot, giving 足 its meaning 'foot, to be sufficient.'

example.hanzi: 足球是世界上最受欢迎的运动。
example.pinyin: Zúqiú shì shìjiè shàng zuì shòu huānyíng de yùndòng.
example.english: Football (soccer) is the most popular sport in the world.
example.fact: Football, known as soccer in some countries, is widely considered the most popular sport in the world, with fans on every continent.

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 态 relates to one's inner state, manner, or attitude
太 (tài) gives the sound — 态 is also pronounced tài, an exact match

example.hanzi: 水有固态,液态,和气态。
example.pinyin: Shuǐ yǒu gùtài, yètài, hé qìtài.
example.english: Water has a solid state, a liquid state, and a gas state.
example.fact: Water is one of the few common substances that people regularly see in all three states of matter: solid ice, liquid water, and gas (steam or vapor).

etymologyHint: Guarding 扌 a home 户; 户 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 扌 (hand) — represents the act of guarding or defending.
户 (door/household) — protecting one's home gave 护 its meaning 'to protect, guard.'

example.hanzi: 很多国家保护野生动物。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō guójiā bǎohù yěshēng dòngwù.
example.english: Many countries protect wild animals.
example.fact: Many countries have laws and nature reserves specifically designed to protect endangered wild animals.

example.hanzi: 七夕节是中国的情人节。
example.pinyin: Qīxījié shì Zhōngguó de qíngrénjié.
example.english: The Qixi Festival is China's Valentine's Day.
example.fact: The Qixi Festival, sometimes called Chinese Valentine's Day, takes place on the seventh day of the seventh lunar month and is based on a romantic folk legend.

example.hanzi: 过年放烟花,大家都很高兴。
example.pinyin: Guònián fàng yānhuā, dàjiā dōu hěn gāoxìng.
example.english: Setting off fireworks at New Year makes everyone happy.
example.fact: Fireworks were invented in ancient China, and setting them off to celebrate festivals like Chinese New Year is a tradition that continues today.

example.hanzi: 孔子是儒家学派的创始人。
example.pinyin: Kǒngzǐ shì Rújiā xuépài de chuàngshǐrén.
example.english: Confucius was the founder of the Confucian school of thought.
example.fact: Confucius founded Confucianism, a school of thought that has profoundly shaped Chinese culture, ethics, and education for over two thousand years.

components.note: 子 (child) — 孩 relates directly to children
亥 (hài) gives a sound close to 孩's reading hái

example.hanzi: 小孩子学语言的速度很快。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi xué yǔyán de sùdù hěn kuài.
example.english: Young children learn languages very quickly.
example.fact: Children have a remarkable natural ability to learn languages quickly, especially before puberty, which is often called the 'critical period' for language acquisition.

components.note: 马 (horse) — 验 originally related to examining or testing horses, later extended to 'to test, examine, verify'
佥 (qiān) gives a loose sound connection to 验's reading yàn

example.hanzi: 科学家做实验,验证自己的想法。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā zuò shíyàn, yànzhèng zìjǐ de xiǎngfǎ.
example.english: Scientists conduct experiments to verify their ideas.
example.fact: Testing ideas through experiments is a core part of the scientific method, used by scientists worldwide to check whether their theories are correct.

etymologyHint: Money 贝 that must be repaid

components.note: 责 shows 贝 (money, a cowry shell) at its base, tied to a debt that must be repaid — giving 责 its meaning 'duty, responsibility, to blame.'

example.pinyin: Yīshēng duì bìngrén de jiànkāng fùzé.
example.english: Doctors are responsible for patients' health.
example.fact: Being responsible for patient health and safety is a core duty at the heart of medical ethics around the world.

example.hanzi: 鸡蛋有很多营养。
example.pinyin: Jīdàn yǒu hěn duō yíngyǎng.
example.english: Eggs have a lot of nutrition.
example.fact: Eggs are considered one of the most nutritionally complete foods, containing protein along with many vitamins and minerals.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 星 relates to bright heavenly bodies like the sun and stars
生 (shēng) gives a sound close to 星's reading xīng

example.hanzi: 火星是红色的星球。
example.pinyin: Huǒxīng shì hóngsè de xīngqiú.
example.english: Mars is a red planet.
example.fact: Mars appears red because its surface is covered in iron oxide, essentially rust, which gives the planet its distinctive color.

components.note: 多 (more/many) — 够 relates to having a sufficient amount
句 (jù) gives a loose sound connection to 够's reading gòu

example.hanzi: 医生说,人每天需要睡够七八个小时。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō, rén měitiān xūyào shuì gòu qī-bā ge xiǎoshí.
example.english: Doctors say people need about seven to eight hours of sleep every day.
example.fact: Sleep experts generally recommend that adults get around seven to eight hours of sleep a night for good health.

etymologyHint: The ten 十 movements of a piece of music 音

components.note: 音 (sound/music) — represents a musical piece.
十 (ten) — ten musical movements or sections making up a complete piece gave 章 its meaning 'chapter, section, composition.'

example.hanzi: 《西游记》有很多章。
example.pinyin: 《Xīyóujì》 yǒu hěn duō zhāng.
example.english: Journey to the West has many chapters.
example.fact: Journey to the West is one of the Four Great Classical Novels of Chinese literature, a very long story told across many chapters.

etymologyHint: A tongue 立 forming a sound in the mouth 日

components.note: 立 here depicts a tongue positioned to speak.
日 here depicts an open mouth — a tongue forming sound in the mouth gave 音 its meaning 'sound, tone.'

example.hanzi: 拼音帮助人学习汉字的发音。
example.pinyin: Pīnyīn bāngzhù rén xuéxí Hànzì de fāyīn.
example.english: Pinyin helps people learn the pronunciation of Chinese characters.
example.fact: Pinyin is the official romanization system for Mandarin Chinese, created in the 1950s to help people learn standard pronunciation.

components.note: 足 (foot) — 跟 originally referred to the heel of the foot, extended to mean 'to follow (on someone's heels)'
艮 (gèn) gives a loose sound connection to 跟's reading gēn

example.hanzi: 小雁跟着妈妈飞。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo yàn gēnzhe māma fēi.
example.english: Baby geese follow their mother when flying.
example.fact: Many baby birds, including geese and ducks, instinctively follow their mother right after hatching — a behavior scientists call imprinting.

etymologyHint: The mind 心 of a scholar 士; 士 also provides the pronunciation

example.pinyin: Hěn duō rén dāng zhìyuànzhě bāngzhù biéren.
example.english: Many people become volunteers to help others.
example.fact: Volunteering, giving time to help others without pay, is a common way people support their communities all around the world.

components.note: 广 (a building/shelter) — 底 relates to the base or bottom, as of a structure
氐 (dǐ) gives the sound — 底 is also pronounced dǐ, an exact match

example.pinyin: Mǎlǐyànà Hǎigōu shì hǎidǐ zuì shēn de dìfang.
example.english: The Mariana Trench is the deepest place at the bottom of the ocean.
example.fact: The Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean is the deepest known part of the world's oceans.

components.note: 立 (to stand) — 站 relates to standing, and by extension a stop or station where one stands to wait
占 (zhàn) gives the sound — 站 is also pronounced zhàn, an exact match

example.hanzi: 北京火车站每天有很多人。
example.pinyin: Běijīng huǒchēzhàn měitiān yǒu hěn duō rén.
example.english: Beijing Railway Station has many people every day.
example.fact: Beijing is a major hub in China's railway network, and its stations see huge numbers of travelers every day, especially during holidays.

example.hanzi: 老师对学生的要求很严格。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī duì xuéshēng de yāoqiú hěn yángé.
example.english: Teachers are strict in their requirements for students.
example.fact: In many East Asian education systems, teachers are traditionally expected to hold students to strict, disciplined standards.

example.hanzi: 埃菲尔铁塔在巴黎。

components.note: 阝 (a mound/wall) — 防 relates to defensive walls and prevention

example.pinyin: Chángchéng shì gǔdài Zhōngguó de guófáng jiànzhù.
example.english: The Great Wall was an ancient Chinese defense structure.
example.fact: The Great Wall was built over many centuries mainly to defend Chinese states and empires from invasions from the north.

etymologyHint: A group of people that swear by 矢 a single flag 方

components.note: 方 (a flag/banner) — a shared banner under which a group gathers.
矢 (arrow) — warriors bound by oath under one flag gave 族 its meaning 'clan, ethnic group, tribe.'

example.pinyin: Zhōngguó yǒu wǔshíliù ge mínzú.
example.english: China has fifty-six ethnic groups.
example.fact: China officially recognizes fifty-six different ethnic groups, with the Han majority alongside many others such as the Tibetan, Uyghur, and Zhuang peoples.

meanings: to be for (the use or convenience of)
etymologyHint: A person 亻 making an offering with both hands 共; 共 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 亻 (person) — the one making an offering.
共 (together/both hands) — a person offering something with both hands gave 供 its meaning 'to supply, provide, offer.'

example.hanzi: 太阳能可以提供清洁的能源。
example.pinyin: Tàiyángnéng kěyǐ tígōng qīngjié de néngyuán.
example.english: Solar energy can provide clean energy.
example.fact: Solar panels convert sunlight directly into electricity, making solar power one of the cleanest renewable energy sources available.

components.note: 攵 (an action/to strike) — 效 relates to the result produced by an action
交 (jiāo) gives a sound close to 效's reading xiào

example.pinyin: Yìmiáo duì yùfáng jíbìng hěn yǒuxiào.
example.english: Vaccines are very effective at preventing disease.
example.fact: Vaccines work by training the body's immune system to recognize and fight specific diseases, and they have been one of the most effective tools in public health history.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 续 relates to continuing, like an unbroken thread
卖 (mài) gives a loose sound connection to 续's reading xù

example.pinyin: Dìqiú yìzhí jìxù rào zhe tàiyáng zhuàn.
example.english: The Earth continues to revolve around the sun.
example.fact: The Earth continuously orbits the Sun, taking about 365 days to complete one full trip — the basis for our calendar year.

example.hanzi: 长城的施工用了很长时间。
example.pinyin: Chángchéng de shīgōng yòngle hěn cháng shíjiān.
example.english: Construction of the Great Wall took a very long time.
example.fact: The Great Wall wasn't built all at once — different sections were constructed and connected over many centuries by different Chinese dynasties.

example.hanzi: 很多中国学生去国外留学。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō Zhōngguó xuésheng qù guówài liúxué.
example.english: Many Chinese students go abroad to study.
example.fact: China sends more students to study abroad than any other country in the world.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讲 relates to speaking, explaining, telling
井 (jǐng) gives a sound close to 讲's reading jiǎng

example.hanzi: 奶奶给孙子讲嫦娥的故事。
example.pinyin: Nǎinai gěi sūnzi jiǎng Cháng'é de gùshì.
example.english: Grandma tells her grandson the story of Chang'e.
example.fact: Chang'e is the goddess of the Moon in Chinese mythology, and her story is traditionally told during the Mid-Autumn Festival.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 型 originally related to a mold made of clay used for casting
刑 (xíng) gives the sound — 型 is also pronounced xíng, an exact match

example.hanzi: 中国古代的青铜器是用模型铸造的。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó gǔdài de qīngtóngqì shì yòng móxíng zhùzào de.
example.english: Ancient Chinese bronze vessels were cast using molds.
example.fact: Ancient Chinese bronze casting, especially during the Shang and Zhou dynasties, produced some of the most sophisticated bronze vessels in the ancient world.

etymologyHint: A hand measuring 斗 a cup of rice 米

components.note: 米 (rice) — the grain being measured.
斗 (a measuring ladle) — measuring out rice gave 料 its meaning 'material, to estimate, to reckon.'

example.hanzi: 海洋里有很多塑料垃圾。
example.pinyin: Hǎiyáng lǐ yǒu hěn duō sùliào lājī.
example.english: There is a lot of plastic waste in the ocean.
example.fact: Plastic pollution is a serious problem in the world's oceans, harming marine animals that mistake it for food.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 终 originally referred to the end of a woven thread, extended to mean 'end, final'
冬 (dōng) gives a loose sound connection to 终's reading zhōng

example.hanzi: 长城的终点在山海关。
example.pinyin: Chángchéng de zhōngdiǎn zài Shānhǎiguān.
example.english: The end of the Great Wall is at Shanhai Pass.
example.fact: The eastern end of the Great Wall is traditionally marked at Shanhai Pass, where the wall meets the sea.

meanings: bound form having the same meaning as the free word 答[da2], used in 答應|答应[da1 ying5], 答理[da1 li5] etc

example.english: At the Lantern Festival, everyone answers lantern riddles together.
example.fact: Guessing riddles written on lanterns is a traditional activity during the Lantern Festival, which marks the end of Chinese New Year celebrations.

components.note: 糸 (silk/thread) — 紧 relates to something pulled taut, as thread is pulled tight when spun, giving its meaning 'tight, tense'

example.pinyin: Zǒu gāngsī de shíhou, shéngzi yào hěn jǐn.
example.english: When walking a tightrope, the rope must be very tight.
example.fact: Tightrope walking requires the rope or wire to be pulled extremely tight and stable so the performer can balance on it safely.

components.note: 黄 originally depicted a large ornamental jade pendant worn at the waist; the character was later borrowed for the color 'yellow.'

example.hanzi: 黄河的水是黄色的。
example.pinyin: Huánghé de shuǐ shì huángsè de.

example.hanzi: 和尚喜欢打坐。
example.pinyin: Héshang xǐhuan dǎzuò.
example.english: Monks like to sit in meditation.
example.fact: Sitting meditation, called dazuo, is a traditional practice in Buddhism used to calm the mind and build focus.

etymologyHint: An altar on which a sacrifice is being made

components.note: 帝 depicts an altar stand used for sacrificial offerings to the gods — the one who presides over such rites came to be known as 帝, 'supreme ruler, emperor.'

example.hanzi: 秦始皇是中国第一个皇帝。
example.pinyin: Qín Shǐhuáng shì Zhōngguó dì yī ge huángdì.
example.english: Qin Shi Huang was China's first emperor.
example.fact: Qin Shi Huang unified China and became its first emperor in 221 BCE, also ordering the construction of the early Great Wall and the Terracotta Army.

components.note: 阝 (a mound/place) — 限 relates to a boundary or limit on a place
艮 (gèn) gives a loose sound connection to 限's reading xiàn

example.hanzi: 开车要遵守限速。
example.pinyin: Kāichē yào zūnshǒu xiànsù.
example.english: When driving, you must obey the speed limit.
example.fact: Speed limits exist in almost every country to help keep roads safe for drivers and pedestrians.

components.note: 舟 (boat) — 船 is a vessel that travels on water, directly tied to its meaning 'ship, boat'

example.hanzi: 中国古代的船有水密舱。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó gǔdài de chuán yǒu shuǐmì cāng.
example.english: Ancient Chinese ships had watertight compartments.
example.fact: Ancient Chinese shipbuilders were among the first to use watertight compartments, a design that kept ships from sinking even if part of the hull was damaged.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — 脸 relates to the face, a part of the body
佥 (qiān) gives a loose sound connection to 脸's reading liǎn

example.hanzi: 京剧演员会在脸上画脸谱。
example.pinyin: Jīngjù yǎnyuán huì zài liǎn shàng huà liǎnpǔ.
example.english: Peking opera performers paint facial patterns on their faces.
example.fact: In Peking opera, the colors and patterns painted on a performer's face, called lianpu, indicate the character's personality and role.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — an old link between listening to official duties and 职's meaning 'duty, profession, office'
只 (zhī) gives a loose sound connection to 职's reading zhí

example.hanzi: 宇航员是一种特别的职业。
example.pinyin: Yǔhángyuán shì yì zhǒng tèbié de zhíyè.
example.english: Astronaut is a special profession.
example.fact: Being an astronaut is one of the rarest professions in the world — only a small number of people have ever traveled to space.

components.note: 辶 (to walk/move) — 速 relates to the speed of movement
束 (shù) gives a loose sound connection to 速's reading sù

example.hanzi: 猎豹是世界上速度最快的陆地动物。
example.pinyin: Lièbào shì shìjiè shàng sùdù zuì kuài de lùdì dòngwù.
example.english: The cheetah is the fastest land animal in the world.
example.fact: Cheetahs can accelerate faster than most sports cars, making them the fastest land animals on Earth.

components.note: 刂 (a knife) — 刻 relates to carving with a blade
亥 (hài) is the historical phonetic element; it no longer closely matches 刻's modern reading kè

example.hanzi: 龙门石窟有很多石刻的佛像。
example.pinyin: Lóngmén Shíkū yǒu hěn duō shíkè de fóxiàng.
example.english: The Longmen Grottoes have many carved stone Buddha statues.
example.fact: The Longmen Grottoes in China contain thousands of carved Buddhist statues cut into stone cliffs, created over hundreds of years.

etymologyHint: Simplified form of 樂, a musical instrument with wood 木, strings 幺, and a pick 白

components.note: 乐 is the simplified form of 樂, which depicted a wooden 木 instrument strung with strings 幺, played with a pick 白 — music came to represent joy, giving 乐 its meaning 'happy, music.'

example.hanzi: 音乐可以让人快乐。
example.pinyin: Yīnyuè kěyǐ ràng rén kuàilè.
example.english: Music can make people happy.
example.fact: Listening to music can boost mood and reduce stress, an effect found in cultures all around the world.

components.note: 不 (not) — 否 relates directly to negation and denial
口 (kǒu) gives a loose sound connection to 否's reading fǒu

example.hanzi: 他问我是否喜欢中国菜。
example.pinyin: Tā wèn wǒ shìfǒu xǐhuan Zhōngguó cài.
example.english: He asked me whether I like Chinese food.
example.fact: 是否 is a formal way to ask 'whether or not' in Mandarin, often used in written Chinese and polite questions.

components.note: 刂 (a knife, related to 刀) — ties to 刚's meaning 'firm, hard, strong'
冈 (gāng) gives the sound — 刚 is also pronounced gāng, an exact match

example.hanzi: 我刚到北京。
example.pinyin: Wǒ gāng dào Běijīng.
example.english: I just arrived in Beijing.
example.fact: 刚 (or 刚才/刚刚) is commonly used before a verb to mean an action happened 'just now, a moment ago' — one of the most common ways to talk about the recent past in Mandarin.

etymologyHint: Dominating a woman 女 by force of arms 戈

components.note: 戌 (a halberd/weapon) — represents armed force.
女 (woman) — force used to intimidate gave 威 its meaning 'power, might, awe-inspiring.'

example.hanzi: 台风的威力很大。
example.pinyin: Táifēng de wēilì hěn dà.
example.english: Typhoons have great power.
example.fact: Typhoons are powerful tropical storms that regularly form over the Pacific Ocean and can bring destructive winds and heavy rain to East Asia.

example.hanzi: 羊毛可以做很暖的衣服。
example.pinyin: Yángmáo kěyǐ zuò hěn nuǎn de yīfu.
example.english: Wool can be used to make very warm clothes.
example.fact: Wool, the fiber that grows as sheep's fur, is naturally excellent at trapping heat, which is why it has been used to make warm clothing for thousands of years.

components.note: 犬 (dog) — an old, now-opaque link behind 状's meaning 'form, shape, condition'
丬 (qiáng) gives a loose sound connection to 状's reading zhuàng

example.hanzi: 雪花的形状都不一样。
example.pinyin: Xuěhuā de xíngzhuàng dōu bù yíyàng.
example.english: Every snowflake's shape is different.
example.fact: Because of the way ice crystals form, snowflakes are said to each have a unique shape, though they typically share the same six-sided symmetry.

etymologyHint: A string 幺 vibrating in an instrument 亠十

components.note: 率 originally depicted a twisted cord or string 幺 being pulled taut in a frame — later extended to meanings like 'to lead' (pulling something along) and 'rate, ratio.'

example.hanzi: 成年人的心率一般是每分钟六十到一百次。
example.pinyin: Chéngnián rén de xīnlǜ yìbān shì měi fēnzhōng liùshí dào yìbǎi cì.
example.english: An adult's heart rate is generally 60 to 100 beats per minute.
example.fact: A normal resting heart rate for a healthy adult usually falls between 60 and 100 beats per minute.

meanings: to exceed; to be more than

example.hanzi: 他很忙,甚至没有时间吃饭。
example.pinyin: Tā hěn máng, shènzhì méiyǒu shíjiān chīfàn.
example.english: He's so busy that he doesn't even have time to eat.
example.fact: 甚至 is used to add an extreme or surprising example, similar to saying 'even' in English — as in 'so busy that he doesn't even have time to eat.'

components.note: 犭 (dog) — an old link behind 独's meaning 'alone, single, solitary'
虫 (chóng) gives a loose sound connection to 独's reading dú

example.hanzi: 熊猫喜欢独自生活。
example.pinyin: Xióngmāo xǐhuan dúzì shēnghuó.
example.english: Pandas like to live alone.
example.fact: Unlike many animals, giant pandas are mostly solitary and prefer to live and forage alone rather than in groups.

meanings: ball used for playing games (variant of 球[qiu2])

components.note: 王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — 球 originally referred to a round piece of jade, extended to mean 'ball, sphere'
求 (qiú) gives the sound — 球 is also pronounced qiú, an exact match

example.hanzi: 地球是圆的。
example.pinyin: Dìqiú shì yuán de.
example.english: The Earth is round.
example.fact: The Earth is roughly a sphere, a fact confirmed by centuries of astronomical observation and, more recently, by photos taken from space.

etymologyHint: Using a tool 殳 to sort items on a tray 舟

components.note: 舟 (boat/tray) — represents a vessel or tray holding items.
殳 (a hand with a tool) — sorting or moving items on a tray gave 般 its meaning 'sort, kind, manner.'

example.hanzi: 一般来说,猫比狗更独立。
example.pinyin: Yìbān lái shuō, māo bǐ gǒu gèng dúlì.
example.english: Generally speaking, cats are more independent than dogs.
example.fact: Compared with dogs, cats are generally considered more independent animals that need less constant attention from their owners.

etymologyHint: Everyone 並 under the sun 日

components.note: 並 (side by side, together) — represents everyone, all people.
日 (sun) — everyone standing together under the same sun gave 普 its meaning 'universal, general, widespread.'

example.hanzi: 普通话是中国的官方语言。
example.pinyin: Pǔtōnghuà shì Zhōngguó de guānfāng yǔyán.
example.english: Mandarin (Putonghua) is China's official language.
example.fact: Putonghua, meaning 'common speech,' is the standard form of Mandarin promoted across China to help speakers of different regional dialects communicate.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 怕 relates to a feeling of fear in one's heart
白 (bái) gives a loose sound connection to 怕's reading pà

example.hanzi: 很多人怕蜘蛛。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō rén pà zhīzhū.
example.english: Many people are afraid of spiders.
example.fact: Fear of spiders, called arachnophobia, is one of the most common phobias among people around the world.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — 弹 relates to a projectile shot from a bow, like a pellet
单 (dān) gives a loose sound connection to 弹's reading dàn

example.hanzi: 枪的子弹速度很快。
example.pinyin: Qiāng de zǐdàn sùdù hěn kuài.
example.english: A gun's bullet travels very fast.
example.fact: Many bullets travel faster than the speed of sound, which is why the crack of a passing bullet can be heard before the gunshot itself.

meanings: to check; to collate; to proofread

components.note: 木 (wood) — 校 originally related to a wooden framework, later coming to mean 'school,' a place of structured learning
交 (jiāo) gives a sound close to 校's reading xiào

example.hanzi: 岳麓书院是中国很古老的学校。
example.pinyin: Yuèlù Shūyuàn shì Zhōngguó hěn gǔlǎo de xuéxiào.
example.english: Yuelu Academy is a very old school in China.
example.fact: Yuelu Academy, founded over a thousand years ago, is one of the oldest institutions of learning in Chinese history and is still part of a university today.

components.note: 艹 (grass/plant) — 苦 relates to the bitter taste of certain plants and herbs
古 (gǔ) gives a sound close to 苦's reading kǔ

example.hanzi: 苦瓜吃起来很苦。
example.pinyin: Kǔguā chī qǐlai hěn kǔ.
example.english: Bitter melon tastes very bitter.
example.fact: Bitter melon is a vegetable common in Asian cooking that is known and named for its distinctly bitter taste.

meanings: to initiate; to create; to achieve (sth for the first time)

components.note: 刂 (a knife) — 创 relates to cutting or wounding, extended to mean 'to start, to create,' as a fresh cut marks a new beginning
仓 (cāng) gives a loose sound connection to 创's reading chuàng

example.hanzi: 中国古代人创造了造纸术。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó gǔdài rén chuàngzàole zàozhǐshù.
example.english: Ancient Chinese people created papermaking.
example.fact: Papermaking is one of ancient China's Four Great Inventions, and it later spread around the world, transforming how information was recorded and shared.

etymologyHint: A false 叚 person 亻; 叚 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 亻 (person) — represents a human figure.

叚 depicts borrowing or handing something over — a person who is not genuine, or something borrowed rather than real, gave 假 its meaning 'false, fake' (and, for a break from routine, 'vacation, leave.')

example.hanzi: 蜡像馆里的人像是假的。
example.pinyin: Làxiàngguǎn lǐ de rénxiàng shì jiǎ de.
example.english: The figures in a wax museum are fake.
example.fact: Wax museums create lifelike fake statues of celebrities and historical figures out of wax, some so realistic that visitors mistake them for real people.

example.hanzi: 乌龟可以活很久。
example.pinyin: Wūguī kěyǐ huó hěn jiǔ.
example.english: Turtles can live for a very long time.
example.fact: Some tortoise species are known to live over one hundred years, making them among the longest-living animals on Earth.

etymologyHint: Gold 钅 that once was 昔 but is lost

components.note: 钅 (metal/gold) — represents something valuable.
昔 (formerly, in the past) — valuable metal that has been mishandled or lost over time gave 错 its meaning 'mistake, wrong.'

example.hanzi: 有时候,犯错可以帮助人学习。
example.pinyin: Yǒu shíhou, fàn cuò kěyǐ bāngzhù rén xuéxí.
example.english: Sometimes, making mistakes can help people learn.
example.fact: Educational research shows that making and correcting mistakes is a natural and valuable part of how people learn new skills.

meanings: Cheng (c. 2000 BC), third of the legendary Flame Emperors 炎帝[Yan2 di4] descended from Shennong 神農|神农[Shen2 nong2] Farmer God
etymologyHint: Three hands 手 lifting a dead body 了

components.note: 承 depicts multiple hands supporting and lifting something from below — giving 承 its meaning 'to support, to receive, to inherit.'

example.hanzi: 书法是中国人传承的艺术。
example.pinyin: Shūfǎ shì Zhōngguó rén chuánchéng de yìshù.
example.english: Calligraphy is an art passed down by Chinese people.
example.fact: Chinese calligraphy has been practiced and passed down for thousands of years and is considered one of the highest traditional art forms in Chinese culture.

etymologyHint: A hand 爪 stamping a seal 卩

components.note: 爪 (a hand/claw) — pressing down.
卩 depicts a seal or stamp — a hand pressing a seal down gave 印 its meaning 'to print, seal, stamp.'

example.hanzi: 印刷术是中国古代的发明。
example.pinyin: Yìnshuāshù shì Zhōngguó gǔdài de fāmíng.
example.english: Printing was an ancient Chinese invention.
example.fact: Printing, including early woodblock printing and later movable type, is one of ancient China's Four Great Inventions, which greatly changed how books were made and shared.
